dedupe_keys.name: iwmi index based flood insurance ibfi pilots in bihar india ex post evaluations of the 2017 and second pilots

description: Two evaluation reports on pilots of an index-based flood insurance product for smallholder farmers in Bihar, India. The CGSpace record of the first report (Aheeyar, de Silva and Senaratna Sellamuttu, 2019, 31 pages) says IWMI built the product from flood modelling and satellite imagery, so that payouts need no individual loss assessment, and tested it with 200 farmers in six villages of Gaighat block, Muzaffarpur district, in the 2017 kharif season; the evaluation used a qualitative assessment in April 2018 and a household survey in July 2018 to draw lessons on making index insurance inclusive and scaling it up. The second report (October 2020, 24 pages) evaluates the second pilot, asking how well the product reached different groups of farmers and what barriers to inclusion remain. Both are free downloadable PDFs marked open access but copyrighted with all rights reserved. Coverage is Muzaffarpur district, Bihar. Caveats: the payout triggers and flood model details are in other IWMI papers, not the pages read. For simulation it shows how a remote-sensing flood trigger can pay farmers after floods, a recovery channel for rural economies. A related catalogue record is the COACCH riverine flood insurance indicators for EU regions.
